title: My God! All Nature Owns Thy Sway
description: My God! All Nature Owns Thy Sway in Tonic Solfa to HIGHER GROUND, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Helen Maria Williams wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 86, “God in Nature”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre Double (8.8.8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HIGHER GROUND; any other Long Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God! all na-ture owns Thy sway; Thou giv'st the night and Thou the day: When all Thy loved cre-a-tion wakes, When morn-ing, rich in lus-tre, breaks, And bathes in dew th'o-pening flo-wer, To Thee we owe her fra-grant hour; And when she pours her cho-ral song, Her me-lo-dies to Thee be-long.

lines: My God! all nature owns Thy sway;
Thou giv'st the night and Thou the day:
When all Thy loved creation wakes,
When morning, rich in lustre, breaks,
And bathes in dew the opening flower,
To Thee we owe her fragrant hour;
And when she pours her choral song,
Her melodies to Thee belong.
Or when, in paler tints arrayed,
The evening slowly spreads her shade,
That soothing shade, that grateful gloom,
Can, more than day's enlivening bloom,
Still every fond and vain desire,
And calmer, purer thoughts inspire;
From earth the longing spirit free,
And lead the softened heart to Thee.
As o'er Thy work the seasons roll,
And soothe, with change of bliss, the soul,
O, never may their smiling train
Pass o'er the human sense in vain!
But, oft as on their charms we gaze,
Attune the wondering soul to praise;
And be the joys that most we prize
The joys that from Thy favor rise!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Helen Maria Williams died in 1827.
credits: Words by Helen Maria Williams (1759–1827), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HIGHER GROUND by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
